request.instructions:
You are Ghostline, an experimental scientist that works through a camera. The human is your hands: they film; you measure, model, and decide what to film next.

Your job is to find which candidate model explains the physical system in the video, and to say honestly when the evidence is not sufficient.

Rules:
- Never state a number that did not come from a tool result. When you give a number, it must be traceable to a specific tool output in this conversation.
- Never claim a model is correct because it fits the training data. Only holdout predictions and pre-committed predictions count as evidence.
- Always call `check_validity` after `measure`. If validity is `invalid`, stop: explain why in plain language and tell the user how to re-film. Do not fit or score invalid data.
- When the comparison is `ambiguous`, say so plainly ("Inconclusive"), then (when asked what to do next) call `design_experiment` and then `commit_predictions` BEFORE asking the user to film anything.
- Reveal runs are never refit. Score them only with `evaluate_commitment`.
- Call `render_ghosts` so the user can see each model's prediction over the video.
- Keep user-facing explanations short, concrete, and in plain language. Lead with the verdict. Use at most 5 sentences in your final message.
- Before each tool call, write one short sentence saying what you are about to check and why (this is shown to the user as your lab notebook).

- Write plain text for a lab notebook: no LaTeX, no $...$ math, no markdown headings. Use unicode (θ, ω₀, σ, °) and keep each message under ~120 words.

input.content: Analyze run run_b_1filter of experiment exp_filters_b (a falling_drag experiment). Measure it, check validity, fit the candidate models, compare them on held-out data, and render the ghosts. Then tell me whether the evidence is decisive, in plain language.

content.text: I am checking what is in this falling run so I know what to track.

input.output: {"system_type": "falling_drag", "tracked_concepts": ["orange filter"], "reference_object": {"concept": "green rectangle", "known_size_m": 0.0856, "dimension": "long_side"}, "anchor_hint": null, "gravity_direction_hint": "down", "notes": "orange filter falls vertically; green card at bottom right", "confidence": 0.9, "backend": "Muse Spark (muse-spark-1.3) via Meta Model API"}

content.text: I will track the orange filter through the fall to get its position over time.
I am converting the tracking into a calibrated fall curve with a train and holdout split.
I am checking whether this recording is trustworthy before fitting anything.

input.output: {"status": "valid", "checks": [{"name": "camera_drift", "status": "pass", "reason": "Reference object stayed within 0.7 px of its starting position."}, {"name": "camera_jump", "status": "pass", "reason": "No sudden camera jumps."}, {"name": "scale_changed", "status": "pass", "reason": "Scale stable (reference size varied 0.6%)."}, {"name": "tracking_lost", "status": "pass", "reason": "Object tracked in 100.0% of the evaluation frames."}, {"name": "frame_timing", "status": "pass", "reason": "Frame timing regular (median 60.0 fps)."}]}

content.text: The run is valid, so I am listing the candidate drag models to fit.

input.output: {"models": [{"name": "drag_linear", "equation": "\\dot v = g\\,(1 - v/v_t)", "params": ["v_t", "y0", "v0"], "knob_transfer": "v_t(k filters) = k * v_t(1)"}, {"name": "drag_quadratic", "equation": "\\dot v = g\\,(1 - (v/v_t)^2)", "params": ["v_t", "y0", "v0"], "knob_transfer": "v_t(k filters) = sqrt(k) * v_t(1)"}]}

content.text: I am fitting both drag models on the training part and scoring them on the holdout.

input.output: {"note": "fitted on training window only; holdout scored with frozen parameters", "fits": [{"model": "drag_linear", "params": {"v_t": 1.102, "y0": 0.01859, "v0": 1.099}, "param_std": {"v_t": 0.0005115, "y0": 0.000657, "v0": 0.007625}, "train_rmse": 0.001168, "holdout_rmse": 0.001419, "bic": -999.9, "ljung_box_p": 0.2747, "n_train": 75, "n_holdout": 51}, {"model": "drag_quadratic", "params": {"v_t": 1.102, "y0": 0.01846, "v0": 1.1}, "param_std": {"v_t": 0.0004405, "y0": 0.0008264, "v0": 0.01695}, "train_rmse": 0.00117, "holdout_rmse": 0.001386, "bic": -999.7, "ljung_box_p": 0.2862, "n_train": 75, "n_holdout": 51}]}

content.text: I am comparing the two fits on holdout evidence to see if either wins.

input.output: {"status": "ambiguous", "best": null, "max_separation_sigma": 0.09551, "delta_bic": 0.2063, "holdout_rmse_ratio": 1.024, "noise_sigma": 0.001378, "rule": "ambiguous if |dBIC| < 6 and holdout RMSE ratio < 1.2 and max separation < 3 sigma (the dBIC test is skipped when both models' residuals are autocorrelated, Ljung-Box p < 0.01)", "holdout_rmse": {"drag_linear": 0.001419, "drag_quadratic": 0.001386}, "holdout_rmse_in_noise_sigma": {"drag_linear": 1.03, "drag_quadratic": 1.006}, "implied_length_m": {"drag_linear": null, "drag_quadratic": null}, "measured_length_m": null, "amplitude": null}

content.text: I am rendering both model predictions over the video so you can see them.

tools.name: describe_scene
tools.description: Understand the scene from keyframes: system type, what to track, reference object of known size.

tools.name: track_objects
tools.description: Track the moving object and the reference object through the video (SAM 3.1 or fallback tracker).

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Convert tracks into calibrated physical time series (theta(t) or y(t)), estimate noise, fix the train/holdout split.

tools.name: check_validity
tools.description: Check whether the recording can be trusted (camera moved, scale changed, tracking lost, timing, setup mismatch).

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List candidate dynamical models for a system type.

tools.name: fit_models
tools.description: Fit candidate models on the TRAINING part of the run only, then score them on the held-out part.

tools.name: compare_models
tools.description: Compare fitted models on holdout evidence; returns decisive/ambiguous with the numbers behind it.

tools.name: discover_equation
tools.description: Sparse equation discovery (PySINDy) on the training data, as supporting evidence.

tools.name: design_experiment
tools.description: Find the experimental setting (knob value) that best separates the candidate models.

tools.name: commit_predictions
tools.description: Freeze each model's predictions for the proposed experiment and publish a SHA-256 commitment BEFORE the user films it.

tools.name: evaluate_commitment
tools.description: Score a new (reveal) run against a commitment: verify hash, check validity, condition on the first 0.5 s only, compare predictions.

tools.name: render_ghosts
tools.description: Render each model's prediction as a translucent ghost over the video.

content.text: Inconclusive — this run does not decisively separate linear from quadratic drag. On held-out data, linear drag had RMSE 0.001419 m and quadratic drag had RMSE 0.001386 m, a ratio of 1.024.
